definitions.explanation: A decorative border or case used to hold and display paintings, photographs, certificates, or other flat items on a wall.

examples.japanese: {絵|え}を{額縁|がくぶち}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put the painting in a frame.

examples.japanese: {木製|もくせい}の{額縁|がくぶち}が{部屋|へや}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}に{合|あ}っている。
examples.english: The wooden frame suits the atmosphere of the room.

examples.japanese: {卒業|そつぎょう}{証書|しょうしょ}を{額縁|がくぶち}に{入|い}れて{壁|かべ}に{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: I framed my diploma and hung it on the wall.

notes:
USAGE:
{額縁|がくぶち} is the standard word for frames used to display artwork, photos, and certificates. It combines {額|がく} (framed picture/plaque) and {縁|ぶち} (border/rim). In architecture, {額縁|がくぶち}{仕上|しあ}げ refers to a frame-like trim around windows or doors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {額縁|がくぶち}に{入|い}れる (to put in a frame)
- {額縁|がくぶち}に{飾|かざ}る (to display in a frame)
- {木製|もくせい}の{額縁|がくぶち} (wooden frame)
- {写真|しゃしん}{立|た}て (photo frame — a related term for tabletop frames)
